Sources indicate that after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw rolled out Moonlock on the Mac, the manufacturer described its newly introduced app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

It has been revealed that in practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Users can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that indicates where apps are sending data and lets users block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the company says “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Industry observers note that unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping people improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets owners quickly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

As MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, users can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

“When we introduced Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

Industry observers note that its intelligent AI sensing algorithm drastically improves reliability by reducing false triggers caused by environmental factors like pets, airflow, and robotic vacuums. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, UPDATED, 5:50 PM: A Los Angeles jury has convicted the man charged with setting the smoldering fire that later flared up into Palisades Fire that devastated Pacific Palisades and Malibu in early 2025. Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, was found guilty Friday of destruction of property by means of fire and arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.

It has been revealed that rinderknecht faces a maximum sentence of 40 years in state prison when he is sentenced on March 17. He has been in federal custody since October 2025. See the bottom of this post for the the Justice Department’s detailed account of Rinderknecht’s movements on the night the first fire started and its case against him.

Back in June, a separate jury deadlocked 10-2 in favor of acquitting Rinderknecht on similar charges including a third for timber set afire. Prosecutors dropped that last charge, and the In the newly introduced indictment, the first charge referred only to Rinderknecht’s setting of the Lachman Fire on New Year’s Eve, rather than the Lachman and Palisades fires. The Lachman Fire smoldered for a week before Santa Ana winds re-ignited the flames. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that during the just-ended trial, Assistant U.S. Attorney Matt O’Brien argued that Rinderknecht was consumed by anger, loneliness and a thirst for revenge, prompting him to use a grill lighter to ignite hilltop vegetation around midnight on Dec. 31, 2024, at the remote, deserted area adjacent to the Pacific Palisades’ Summit neighborhood. But defense lawyer Steven Haney argued there was no direct evidence proving that his client set the earlier fire, saying the prosecution’s case lacked any witnesses to the alleged crime and consisted only of circumstantial allegations.

The Los Angeles Fire Department issued in a statement Friday after the verdict. “We respect the jury’s work and the long, difficult process that brought us to today’s verdict,” it reads in part. “Our first thought is with the families of those we lost and for everyone in our community whose lives were changed by this fire. No verdict, however notable, could ever undo that loss.”.

The Palisades Fire was the most destructive blaze in Los Angeles history, killing 12 people, burning 23,448 acres, costing billions in damage and insurance claims, and ruining much of the exclusive Pacific Palisades community, destroying about 6,500 structures across the Palisades and Malibu. Read more details below, and see the full news release from the U.S. Department of Justice at the bottom of this post.

PREVIOUSLY, June 25: The jury charged with determining if Jonathan Rinderknecht is guilty of starting the blaze in early 2025 that became the devastating Palisades Fire can’t come up with a verdict, yet.

Industry observers note that “The jury in the Jonathan Rinderknecht trial sent a subsequent note saying they are deadlocked,” the Justice Department tells Deadline today. “The trial continues.”.

In a recent development, how long the trial continues now or if a mistrial is declared becomes the vital questions. U.S. District Court Judge Anne Hwang has instructed the jury to return on Friday morning to take another kick at the can.

According to recent reports, A note from the jurors read out in court earlier this afternoon in downtown L.A. by the judge set the stage. “We have people on both sides that are dead set, unwavering and unwilling to change their opinion,” the note, the second of the day, noted. It went on to say: “We are at a standstill and unsure of how to proceed.”.

Ex-Uber driver Rinderknecht has always insisted he is innocent of the charges and being put up as a fall guy for the failures of civic leaders and First Responders. If a mistrial is declared in this instance, the feds could attempt another trial with a fresh jury and hope for a better outcome.

Industry observers note that after just over a day of deliberations on the arson charges after a 10-day trial, the jurors indicated they had a verdict just over 90 minutes ago. The currently incarcerated Rinderknecht, his defense team, prosecutors and various local, state and federal officials were brought into court after the judge was informed there was a “unanimous verdict.”.

What they finally did hear left Judge Hwang in clear angst.

While there was some confusion initially over when their decision would be read out in court, and the clocked ticked away, it is now clear the case is in serious trouble — even as it continues.

Industry observers note that looking at up to 45 years behind bars if found guilty, Rinderknecht was, in Department of Justice documents filed last fall, “indicted on one count of Destruction of Property by Means of Fire (18 U.S.C. § 844(f)(1)); one count of Arson Affecting Property Used in Interstate Commerce (18 U.S.C. § 844(i)); and one count of Timber Set Afire (18 U.S.C. § 1855), in a case arising out of the Lachman/Palisades Fire in January 2025.”.

According to recent reports, today’s verdict or lack there of, will continue the frustration many feel over the wildfires, the response and the consequences. While some reconstruction has taken place in the Palisades, as well as Malibu and out of the Eaton Fire that tore through Altadena, progress has been slow and stymied by all metrics.

Sources indicate that A major factor in the ongoing L.A. mayoral race, and the spark for the unsuccessful insurgency campaign of ex-Palisades resident and Hills alum Spencer Pratt, the fires and the fallout hang heavy over the city and the community as another sign of a metropolis that has lost its way — even more so this past week with the just extinguished cold storage warehouse fire in Boyle Heights that prompted air quality and other health warnings.

Industry observers note that the subject of an intense investigation by various branches of government both national and state, Rinderknecht was arrested in Florida on October 8 last year. The then 29-year-old is accused of intentionally starting a “hold over” fire the week before that eventually sparked into the Palisades Fire.

Placed at the scene by his own iPhone and failed 9-1-1 calls, Rinderknecht later that Newly introduced Year’s Day morning drove away from the area as LAFD started arriving on the scene, making a gesture to assist the firefighters, the DOJ’s filing of last year asserted.

It has been revealed that A week later the same fire, which even after LAFD has been on the scene, had likely smoldered underground, reemerged and became known as the Palisades Fire. Destroying most of the Hollywood heavy community, the Palisades Fire killed more than a dozen people and decimated over 5,400 homes.

Earlier this week, after closing arguments, defense lawyer Steve Haney entered a motion to have the case dismissed based on lack of compelling evidence by the feds. With the bevy of online postings and asking AI platforms if you could start a fire with a lit cigarette, as well as Rinderknecht’s involvement with the January 1, 2025 Lachman Fire that preceded the Palisades Fire, that dismissal effort was dismissed pretty promptly by Judge Hwang.

More such motions from the defense may be in the offering ASAP if this deadlocked situation continues into next week.

Here is the Justice Department’s post-verdict news release:.

According to recent reports, A former Los Angeles resident was found guilty by a jury today of starting what became the Palisades Fire of January 2025, the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.Jonathan Rinderknecht, 30, a.k.a. “Jonathan Rinder,” and “Jon Rinder,” was found guilty of one count of destruction of property by means of fire and one count of arson affecting property used in interstate commerce.“Twelve people lost their lives and thousands lost their homes because of Jonathan Rinderknecht’s malicious conduct,” said Attorney General Todd Blanche. “Thanks to the persistence and hard work of our prosecutors in the Central District of California, he will be held accountable.”“Jonathan Rinderknecht deliberately ignited a fire that killed 12 people and devastated an entire community,” said First Assistant United States Attorney Bill Essayli. “We were determined to hold him accountable, and today’s guilty verdict delivers a measure of justice for the families who lost loved ones and the thousands whose lives were upended.”According to evidence presented at a 14-day trial, on January 1, 2025, Rinderknecht ignited what came to be known as the Lachman and Palisades fires.In the days leading up to the Lachman Fire, Rinderknecht exhibited extreme anger, indignation, and frustration about being unable to find companionship on New Year’s Eve 2024 and about a former co-worker whom he briefly dated in March 2024.Alone on New Year’s Eve, Rinderknecht drove several Uber passengers, nearly all of whom remembered him being angry that night. He dropped off his final Uber passenger in the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles and drove to The Summit, a neighborhood where he had lived a few years earlier with a former lover.Rinderknecht drove towards Skull Rock Trailhead, parked his car, attempted to contact a former friend, and walked up the trail. He then used his iPhone to take videos at a nearby hilltop area and listened to a rap song – to which he had listened repeatedly in previous days – whose music video included things being lit on fire.When Rinderknecht maliciously started the Lachman Fire just after midnight, he was alone in a small clearing on Hidden Buddha Hill in Pacific Palisades.At approximately 12:12 a.m. on January 1, 2025, environmental sensing platforms indicated the Lachman Fire had begun. During the next five minutes, Rinderknecht called 911 several times, but didn’t get through because his iPhone was out of cellphone range. When he finally connected with 911, he was at the bottom of the hiking trail and reported the fire. By that point, a nearby resident already had reported the fire to authorities.Rinderknecht then fled in his car, passing fire engines driving in the opposite direction. He then turned around and followed the fire engines to the scene, driving at a high rate of speed. Rinderknecht walked up the same trail from earlier that night to watch the fire and the firefighters. At approximately 1:02 a.m., he used his iPhone to take more videos of the scene.During an interview with law enforcement on January 24, 2025, Rinderknecht lied about where he was when he first saw the Lachman Fire. He claimed he was near the bottom of a hiking trail when he first saw the fire and called 911, but geolocation data from his iPhone carrier demonstrated that he was standing in a clearing 30 feet from the fire as it rapidly grew.Although firefighters rapidly suppressed the Lachman Fire, the fire continued to smolder and burn underground within the root structure of dense vegetation.On January 7, 2025, heavy winds caused the underground fire to surface and spread above ground in what became known as the Palisades Fire, which caused widespread damage in Pacific Palisades, killing 12 people, and destroyed 6,837 structures, causing an estimated $25 billion in damage in the most destructive wildfire in the city’s history.United States District Judge Anne Hwang scheduled a March 17, 2027 sentencing hearing, at which time Rinderknecht would face a mandatory minimum sentence of five years in federal prison and a statutory maximum sentence of 40 years in federal prison.Rinderknecht has been in federal custody since October 2025.The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives is investigating this matter with substantial assistance from the Los Angeles Police Department and the United States Forest Service.Assistant United States Attorneys Mark A. Williams, Matthew W. O’Brien, and Danbee C. Kim of the Environmental Crimes and Consumer Protection Section are prosecuting this case.If you are a victim of the Palisades Fire, updates about this criminal case can be found on this webpage.

Electronic products now pack circuits, structures, thermal paths, and packaging into very small spaces. These physical domains interact with one another. A packaging choice can change how a shock load reaches a circuit board. Such interactions are hard to predict. Most are found during physical qualification, late in development. At that stage, the design is mostly fixed. A failure leads to redesign, rebuilds, and retesting. Physical tests give strong evidence of robustness, but they give limited insight into load paths and failure margins. Traditional simulation gives more detail, but it needs specialist skills and long manual setup. This white paper explains how guided virtual validation brings shock and drop assessment into the design phase. It reviews common test configurations, model inputs, and acceptance criteria. A packaged drop case study then indicates how packaging can be optimized across all drop orientations and checked against physical test results.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VWFNDR + MBL, an Android camera app that doesn’t overprocess and delivers high-quality DNG (RAW) files, is getting a 2.0 release with improved color grading and an expansion to the iPhone.

VWFNDR + MBL released on Android in May 2026 with a few points that stood out. A unique UI that adapts to the shot, minimal processing for a natural look, and support for DNG files at a level that only Google’s Pixel Camera app can truly compete with.

The app has been downloaded over 300,000 times since then, and is now getting a pretty substantial revision.

On Android, this comes in the form of new color grading profiles built into the app. “NATURAL,” “NIHON,” or “B+W.” The app still saves an unprocessed DNG alongside the JPG and the grading adapts across the frame rather than having a fixed result, keeping highlights and shadows in place.

According to recent reports, colour grades: MBL still records unprocessed Bayer RAW DNG, and the JPG it renders alongside now uses one of three grades: NATURAL, NIHON, or B+W. Grading happens on VWFNDR’s own spatial engine. Instead of applying a fixed LUT, it adapts across the frame, much like a raw editor, so highlights and shadows keep their detail. The DNG stays untouched.

Here’s what the output looks like:.

The rest of VWFNDR + MBL 2.0 takes place off of Android.

It has been revealed that in a rare case of the tables turning, MBL was released first on Android, and only on Android for the first several months. But VWFNDR is now bringing the app to iPhone with support for variable aperture on iPhone 18 Pro and Content Credentials, Apple’s version of the C2PA standard that’s meant to prove a photo is real and not AI-generated.

In a recent development, amazon's Black Friday 2026 sale has brought the Sonos Arc Ultra down to $849 from its usual $1,099, a $250 discount that marks its lowest price yet. PCMag named it the best soundbar of 2024 and gave it an “outstanding” rating in its review. Still, $849 is a lot to spend on a single soundbar, and anyone shopping on a tighter budget will find more affordable picks in our Fire TV soundbar roundup. For more editor-vetted tech deals, check out our comprehensive Black Friday coverage.

It has been revealed that for those who can make room in their budget, the next thing to proposal around is space, since the Arc Ultra measures a little over 46 inches across and weighs about 13 pounds, making it a natural match for a larger TV. Despite all that width, it keeps a low profile at just under three inches tall, so it can sit beneath most screens without blocking the picture, or you can wall-mount it if you would rather keep your TV stand clear. All that size makes room for a 9.1.4-channel layout (a significant step up from the original Arc) that gives Dolby Atmos effects more space to spread around and above you. Sonos also added a new Sound Motion driver that it notes doubles the original Arc's bass, giving action scenes real weight without a separate subwoofer, though you can still add a Sub 4 later for more rumble.

According to recent reports, at the other end of the sound spectrum, voices and dialogue come through clearly even at low volumes, and a Speech Enhancement mode lifts them further. Trueplay tuning then adjusts the sound to your room, with a quick version on Android and iOS and a more detailed one for iPhone owners. The biggest drawback is connectivity, since the Arc Ultra has a single HDMI eARC port with no passthrough, which can leave you short on inputs for a console or streaming box, and no optical port. It also lacks DTS:X support, a letdown for some Blu-ray collectors, and voice control is limited to Alexa or Sonos' own assistant, though Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and AirPlay 2 make streaming music from your phone easy.

#39703. Breaking: Vibecoding an inference chip

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2277 w)

Breaking: Vibecoding an inference chip

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Ankitg

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Or rather, I vibe-coded an FPGA into running an LLM.
  • One of the more entertaining things about programming recently is that coding agents let me work in entirely fresh domains by giving me access to new programming languages and paradigms.
  • I overheard some founders recently talk about how FPGAs work.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Or rather, I vibe-coded an FPGA into running an LLM. And it… just worked.

One of the more entertaining things about programming recently is that coding agents let me work in entirely fresh domains by giving me access to new programming languages and paradigms. Lately, that has meant hacking on hardware, now that writing low-level software is much easier. So, in this blog post, I’m going to try to recount the experience of vibe coding an FPGA, going through a series of “oh shit” moments several times, and giving myself a new appreciation for what’s possible if you have a large token budget (thanks YC) and interesting problems to point the models at.

I overheard some founders recently talk about how FPGAs work. I’ll admit I was relatively naive about them. I’d never really experimented with them in my startup or in college, so I knew little about them before. The basic idea I was familiar with: you can program a circuit into a reprogrammable chip. So rather than having a general purpose computing architecture (like a CPU) you can have a reprogrammable one, i.e. the configuration loaded onto the chip determines how its logic and routing are connected, and that (in theory) enables performance advantages. I also know that it took a mountain of C++ to write and involved manually analyzing waveforms for simulation and verification. I had never done this before though and it seemed cumbersome.

That’s about what I knew going into this.

Naturally, my ML brain thought “could we use these for AI inference”. I’m not the first to think this — there are a few repos attempting to port ML models to FPGAs on Github. But I hadn’t actually seen a writeup on whether coding agents are good at writing the low level C++ and Verilog code to program them and verifying the outputs so that they actually run accurately. (Spoiler alert, they are incredible at programming them.).

So I decided I needed to get my hands on one. AWS has F2 instances with FPGA hardware, and that seemed easier than going and buying physical hardware, so I asked Codex to spin up a reservation and got cooking. It had a relatively limited memory of 16 GB of FPGA HBM. Around the same time, I was working with the DeepGrove founders who were discussing their new ternary weight architecture that is well suited for memory limited cases. It’s SOTA on Mac hardware with actual agentic tool calling, so I figured why not, let’s see if I can get this working on an FPGA and fast enough to be useful.

Sources indicate that what followed was a cloud agent running in Conductor for several days with me mostly just encouraging it periodically while it both (1) got a model fully running and (2) increased its speed by 33× from the first full-model bit-exact baseline to get it to a real-time relevant speed. It was one of the most mind blowing autoresearch loops I’ve run, ultimately writing roughly 3M lines across the experiment history and parsing 30M lines of output files, burning only $10,000 in Claude and OpenAI tokens to run hundreds of experiments. Most of the code is C++ and some Verilog. It’s been probably a decade since the last time I wrote any serious amount of C++ and I’ve never written Verilog. I honestly don’t know the first thing about Verilog. Most of my prompts were not particularly clever: they consisted mostly of me saying things like “you’re a superintelligent model, time to be more creative” and “let’s go for 2x faster, you got this”. Sometimes I brought some ML knowhow like “hey it’s time to consider speculative decoding” or “why is that running on CPU, you should port it”. But for the most part, it was just vibes and I’m pretty sure that with enough time the model would have figured out those things. Also, it seemed that both Astra and Opus (new Fable wasn’t out yet) were pretty capable at this and I could use them interchangeably. I’m sure someone has a good benchmark for which is smarter but both passed my smart-enough threshold.

Measured benchmark tokens/s · select a step to see what changed.

A head loader that reads both of its memory banks at once (+17.3%, measured on and off on one image), a runtime expert-prefetch policy, and the router-job timing fix; run one clock step lower (225/425 MHz) after a soak test found random faults at 231.25.

The chart follows the measured optimization sequence: 6 → 213 tokens/s, or 33× the baseline.

Recent findings suggest that at one point, around when it got to 10 TPS, I messaged the DeepGrove founders about this, and they replied surprised that it was working so easily, saying they had tried this a few months back and the models were not quite good enough to be particularly effective. They sent me a prompt that summarizes some of their lessons and I copy-pasted it into my session to see if it’d matter. It was essentially the most significant piece of actual guidance I added to this session. The prompt is reproduced below.

Recent findings suggest that here is what someone else did for a dense bs=1 decode optimized fpga implementation for a dense qwen style model with ternary weights. you should take this with a grain of salt and pick things that you believe are acutally useful to add to your initiative. Please also dont do things if you dont think is useful that take a lot of times like runnning really long test of a cycle accurate simulation etc or like physical design since those can take like hours. here are some ideas please pick and choose use this as context and not somehting that you shoudl be strictly guided by somethings that could help. prioritiize speed of like getting this up and running though..

Industry observers note that the coding agent diligently considered these asks, but it didn’t seem to make all that much of a difference qualitatively. Indeed, when I asked it later to read all of the logs and determine which of these instructions it actually used, it said:.

Sources indicate that its biggest design ideas were already in my initiative before you pasted it. You pasted it on Oct 29 at 21:50 UTC: 4,741 characters describing what someone else did for a dense, batch-1, ternary FPGA decoder. Within 70 seconds I had sorted it into ten ideas to adopt and five to reject, and written that into every design agent’s brief. The shorter remark from your friend Edward, about using lookup tables as logic gates, came 24 minutes earlier and left nothing on the speed line.

Design ideas I adopted: mostly confirmation.

Already planned: streaming weights straight into the compute lanes, running rows in parallel, and reading the attention cache in bursts were all in the design brief I’d released 35–40 minutes earlier.

Sources indicate that ideas I rejected: all five numerics shortcuts. Lower-precision activations, a deferred norm, an 8-bit KV cache, online softmax and 16-bit probabilities each change the output bits. That is where their design got its efficiency, and your bit-exact rule ruled it out.

Process advice: this changed things right away.

What you asked: not to do things that take hours.

What I stopped: a simulation that had run for about 24 hours, and two 250 MHz builds.

What I switched to: a short loop of C tests, synthesis and a logic-depth check, with one place-and-route per integration.

Likely gain: it got hardware results sooner.

Possible cost, which I can’t prove: two hangs that only RTL simulation could show reached the board the next day, and the significant integration lost 38 hours to them.

Industry observers note that one real find it triggered. While checking their memory ideas, I found AWS’s own reference memory design, which reaches 426 GB/s across all 32 memory channels. The memory subsystem was built from it.

In a recent development, in other words, for most of the actual design ideas it is unclear but there is good reason to believe the model would have figured them out, especially because it came up with them many cycles later after several compaction cycles. But the process advice was useful immediately for getting to hardware results sooner and increasing iteration speed. In other words, the humans are still useful at defining how to iterate fast and what correctness looks like, and the agents are great to manage the exploration.

According to recent reports, here are the changes the autoresearch loop found. Interestingly, it’s mostly a series of modest improvements that compound 1.5x ish every time, rather than one or two giant ones.

Baseline: the first full-model bit-exact FPGA image (R8), served with host-side prefix caching.

Host software only: per-command overhead fell from ~10 ms to 0.9 ms (persistent register mapping, streaming reads, no per-command SDK calls or fsyncs).

1.25× this step · 1.25× from baseline.

A 128-lane attention engine that reads the KV cache in bursts instead of a word at a time, keeping the reference's exact summation order.

1.74× this step · 2.18× from baseline.

A parallel MoE router with an exact GCC-sort tie-breaker plus a streaming output head with built-in argmax; moderate-effort routing let it run at 250 MHz.

1.46× this step · 3.19× from baseline.

A glue engine that parallelizes norms, RoPE, quantization and copies between engines in certified exact orders.

1.47× this step · 4.70× from baseline.

The full fresh pipeline (streaming ternary projection lanes + a new sequencer replacing R8's control path), after fixing two hangs that only appeared in hardware.

1.63× this step · 7.65× from baseline.

Exact speculative decoding: the host drafts tokens by prompt lookup and the FPGA verifies several in one pass.

1.04× this step · 7.97× from baseline.

Fixed a relay that moved router weights between dies at 1/6 speed: router stall per layer 43,862 → 12,292 cycles.

1.14× this step · 9.08× from baseline.

Head shadow v2 (start the next token on a provisional guess; catch misses early) plus cross-die timing fixes, enabling 237.5 MHz kernel / 450 MHz memory.

1.62× this step · 14.68× from baseline.

Exact speculative decoding with a real draft model: a cut-down Maple on the F2's host CPUs drafts ahead, and the FPGA verifies every token.

1.12× this step · 16.42× from baseline.

Doubled the memory ports from 4 to 8 (two projection lanes, output head striped across banks): 1.39× per clock, but congestion cut the clock to 181/375 MHz.

1.03× this step · 16.91× from baseline.

Hid the attention engine's KV fetches behind its compute, and replaced the router's 2,048-step serial sum with an exact order-independent one (12,292 → 2,338 cycles per layer).

1.24× this step · 20.98× from baseline.

Lossless 5-trit weight packing (−20% weight bytes), shorter serial steps, and moving the output head to the far die, which relieved congestion and allowed 225/400 MHz.

1.27× this step · 26.63× from baseline.

Re-speculation after head-shadow misses, speculative MoE expert prefill during the router, and a die rebalance (without the unused DDR controller) that ran 231.25/450 MHz on both boots.

1.08× this step · 28.63× from baseline.

A head loader that reads both of its memory banks at once (+17.3%, measured on and off on one image), a runtime expert-prefetch policy, and the router-job timing fix; run one clock step lower (225/425 MHz) after a soak test found random faults at 231.25.

1.16× this step · 33.13× from baseline.

Recent findings suggest that it’s difficult to do a 1:1 comparison across these configurations. I didn’t run the same autoresearch loop on every alternative, and I assume there is more performance to extract if I did. The point is to show how slow the FPGA was in its first implementation, and how far the optimization loop took it.

The measurements below are from November 15 on AWS, replaying the same 8-chat × 3-turn benchmark. Prices are the on-demand rates recorded with that experiment. “Exact turns” counts outputs that matched the pinned CPU reference. The GPU implementations are included for context but did not satisfy the same bit-exact criterion but are pretty close in practice.

Recent findings suggest that this is one generation starting with a 16-token prompt and continuing until the 8,192-token context is full: 8,176 generated tokens. The five middle columns show decode speed in tokens/s at the indicated context length for several generations of iteration. The last column is wall-clock time for the whole run/.

* For r8 and r9, the first two columns come from separate, shorter runs generating 2,032 tokens. The other columns come from the full-context run.

r9 improves short-context speed, while the complete long-context run is roughly tied with r8.

These examples come from the final r9 image.

246 tokens · 229.7 tokens/s · 1.16 s end to end.

140 tokens · 220.0 tokens/s · 0.76 s end to end.

It has been revealed that system prompt: “You are a helpful assistant. Think briefly before you answer, then reply clearly and concisely.”.

This was a fun project. I’m not sure I’m ever going to use this specific chip architecture in this specific way, and I’m certainly not claiming that an 8,192-token-context model running on an FPGA is the way I’d recommend anyone use something like this in production. But it’s pretty epic that this just works. Capability like this completely shifts the overton window for what a committed team of engineers can work on. It should mean that entirely new types of ideas (scientific discoveries, products, startups) are possible if you can point the models in the right direction. I’m excited to see what everyone builds.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait.
  • According to recent reports, like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro.
  • Industry observers note that so, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto VI offers a size befitting the 13-year wait. Not only is the Vice City map absolutely huge, but it’s the most system-rich and mechanically deep game in the Grand Theft Auto series to date. There’s an overwhelming amount of things to see, do, and learn.

According to recent reports, like millions of gamers worldwide, I dived into the game at midnight, the very second it unlocked on my PS5 Pro. I’ve since put five hours of playtime into GTA 6, and while I’m still getting my head around all that the game has to offer (my completion percentage is a mere 12%), I’ve already learnt a few lessons the hard way. Yes, mistakes have been made.

Industry observers note that so, if you’re heading to Leonida over the weekend, here are three major mistakes I've already made, and most importantly, how you can avoid doing the same stupid things as me (all spoiler-free). Learn from my errors!

It has been revealed that after 13 years of waiting, Grand Theft Auto VI has arrived. Set in the state of Leonida, with Vice City at its heart, you play Jason and Lucia, two criminals forced into an increasingly dangerous situation as they seek their fortune, discovering the darker side of the sunniest spot in America.

GTA 6 introduces a newly introduced money system in which you can hold cash either on your person or stashed securely at your safehouse. If you get “wasted” or “busted” by the cops, you’ll lose all the money you’re carrying, but the funds kept under the floorboards at Jason's beachside home are protected.

Sources indicate that as a cautious type, I took this to mean never carry any money on your person for fear of losing it, which pretty promptly proved to be an oversteer when an early mission required me to buy a gun, and I literally had $0 in my wallet. This forced a trip back to the safehouse, where I counted out the exact number of bills required to buy the weapon.

Once I returned to the Ammu-nation store, I bought my gun and then was presented with a range of attachments (some with a limited-time discount), which I couldn’t buy because, again, I’d only brought the specific amount required to buy the gun itself. Frustrating.

According to recent reports, this taught me not to fear actually carrying money in your wallet. Sure, running about Vice City with your entire bank balance on hand is probably unwise, but you’re going to want, and need, some money in your pocket. At this early stage, I’ve been opting for a 50/50 split, keeping half my ill-gotten gains in my stash, and the other half within instant reach.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

My approach to previous GTA games tended to be this: Complete a few story missions, and then go on a psychotic rampage to blow off some steam (I swear I’m not a total psycho).

GTA 6 is different. For pretty much the first time in the franchise’s history, the game actively discourages you from causing carnage without purpose through the upcoming “Criminal Profile” system. Your in-game actions are tracked and contribute to the type of criminal Jason (and later Lucia) is becoming. Ranging from a “professional” all the way to a full-blown “psycho.”.

During my first GTA 6 session, after completing the mandatory prologue, I decided to see how many wanted stars I could rack up with just the starter pistol, and pretty promptly the game warned me that my criminal spree would have consequences. It felt like that old Tellale’s The Walking Dead warning message, “Clementine will remember that…”.

Rockstar has confirmed your “Criminal Profile” will impact how the story plays out, and I certainly don’t want to receive a “bad” ending; such was my concern about how my early game rampage would impact how my GTA 6 story plays out, I opted to reload to a previous save to instantly wash away the worrying amount of blood already on Jason’s hands.

It has been revealed that so, in GTA 6, it pays to show restraint. You will commit many crimes, of course, but resist the urge to go full GTA and instead commit your criminal acts with purpose and even planning.

Speaking of planning, from what I’ve played so far, GTA 6 is the most ambitious Grand Theft Auto yet in all areas, including mission design. Previous GTA games present players with cinematic but largely linear missions; if you tried to get creative, the game would swiftly shepherd you back onto the golden path with instant fail states for any deviations.

To be clear, GTA 6 does have these types of missions as well, but there’s a larger focus on player choice and letting you pick your approach. As an early (spoiler-free) example, a Chapter 1 mission asks you to retrieve a red sports car from a police impound lot.

It has been revealed that you’re dropped off right outside the main gate, with an on-screen prompt encouraging you to break the lock. Naturally, I obliged, and the impound’s alarms started blaring; every cop in the area was instantly alerted, and the mission pretty much went further south from there.

One reload later, I was back at the mission start, and this time, I slowed down. I cased the joint first, walking the perimeter, trying to find a subtler way to access the impound lot. And what do you know, a conveniently placed scissor lift around the corner got me onto the roof, allowing me to quietly drop into the compound without setting off any alarms or alert cops.

It’s a reminder that in GTA 6, thinking before you act can pay off, and when you factor in the “Criminal Profile” system, there is real merit in completing missions without having to shoot your way out of trouble.

Read on for all the plot details, character casting and more about Presumed Innocent Season 2.

Sources indicate that when will Presumed Innocent Season 2 come out? Watch on Deadline.

In a recent development, in November, Apple unveiled that the second season of the crime drama will premiere February 19, 2027 with its first two episodes. The rest will follow weekly through April 2.

Who will be in the cast of Presumed Innocent Season 2?

Rachel Brosnahan (The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel, Superman) will lead Season 2 of the legal series alongside Jack Reynor (Midsommar, The Perfect Couple, whose casting Deadline reported exclusively. Matthew Rhys (The Americans, Perry Mason)was also cast as a lead in early September 2025, and Fiona Shaw (Bad Sisters, Killing Eve) was cast as a series regular Oct. 1. Still more names include Courtney B. Vance, John Magaro, Michael Hsu Rosen and Lesley-Ann Brandt.

Ji-young Yoo (KPop Demonhunters, Expats) will recur in Season 2 as Deadline revealed in January 2026.

Industry observers note that what happened in Presumed Innocent Season 1? Who was in the cast of Presumed Innocent Season 1?

Season 1 of the series was inspired by Scott Turow’s 1987 courtroom thriller novel of the same name. It starred Jake Gyllenhaal in the main role of Rusty Sabich, the character Harrison Ford played in the 1990 film adaptation of Turow’s best-seller.

Recent findings suggest that the cast of Season 1 also included Bill Camp as Raymond Horgan, Renate Reinsve as Carolyn Polhemus, Ruth Negga as Barbara Sabich, O-T Fagbenle as Nico Della Guardia, Peter Sarsgaard as Tommy Molto, Elizabeth Marvel as Lorraine Horgan, Lily Rabe as Dr. Liz Rush, Chase Infiniti as Jaden Sabich and more.

What will Presumed Innocent Season 2 be about?

As Deadline first reported, Season 2 will be based on Jo Murray’s debut legal thriller Dissection of a Murder, which will publish in 2026. The book centers Leila Reynolds, who is way out of her death when offered her first murder case by a defendant that only wants her. Backblaze is headquartered in the United States and is a data storage organization that provides two primary services. The first, Computer Backup, offers unlimited cloud backup solutions for individuals and organizations using Mac or PC devices, including laptops and desktops. The second, B2 Cloud Storage, provides scalable cloud storage solutions designed to meet the needs of individuals and organizations.

This Privacy Notice explains how Backblaze collects, uses, and shares your personal information when Backblaze acts as a data controller, meaning Backblaze determines the purposes and methods of processing your personal information unless otherwise specified in a separate agreement or required by applicable law. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple only debuted high-end ‘Pro’ and ‘Duo’ iPhones this fall, marking a departure from previous years when more affordable models debuted too. But iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 are still coming, and a newly introduced report offers an update on release timing.

A new report from Kim Yeong-ho at ETNews provides a fresh update on timing for the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2.

Rumors have indicated for well over a year that Apple planned to push these models out of the typical fall launch window and introduce them in early 2027 instead.

Per ETNews, Samsung and LG are providing the display panels for the fresh models, with Samsung the sole supplier for iPhone Air 2 and both companies splitting orders for iPhone 18. And their mass production prepares signal a March release for the products.

Kim Yeong-ho, writing at ETNews:.

Samsung Display plans to begin mass production in January, while LG Display will start late this year…The Korean panel makers appear to be aligning their production plans with an expected March launch.

Industry observers note that A March launch window lines up well with when Apple tends to ramp up product introductions following a slower winter. Earlier this year, iPhone 17e debuted in March alongside latest Macs and the iPad Air.

The year before, however, the iPhone 16e arrived in February instead.

With Apple shaking up its normal iPhone rollout schedule, it was anyone’s guess how soon the fresh models would debut. But a March launch makes sense and gives Apple a trio of new iPhones every six months—three unveiled in September, and another three in March.

Are you holding out for an iPhone 18 or iPhone Air 2? Let us know in the comments.

GTA 6’s 30 FPS lock broke my PC gamer brain — until I turned on the one TV setting I swore I’d never touch

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • If you’ve ever bought a newly introduced TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.
  • According to recent reports, for movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder.
  • And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever bought a newly introduced TV and invited a tech nerd like me into your living room, you already know I’m grabbing your remote, diving into the picture settings, and disabling motion smoothing.

According to recent reports, for movies and prestige TV, it is a crime against humanity — turning a cinematic masterpiece into an episode of "Days of Our Lives" shot on a camcorder. I hate it. Tom Cruise hates it. You should hate it too.

And yet, here I am, playing Grand Theft Auto VI with motion smoothing cranked on, and refusing to turn it off.

It has been revealed that to understand how I ended up committing TV heresy, you have to understand the shock to the system that is GTA 6’s frame rate. Coming straight from my monster PC rig playing games like Resident Evil Requiem at up to 214 FPS, dropping back down to a strict 30 FPS console lock feels like wading through treacle.

Industry observers note that but on top of that, as I’ve seen (and you’ve seen on Digital Foundry’s test), that 30 FPS lock isn’t an actual lock. It can dip into the mid-20s during heavy scenes. Coming from super fluidity, that 30 FPS is brutal to adapt to.

So out of sheer desperation (and because we’re stuck waiting for the PC port), I broke the golden rule and toggled my TV’s smooth motion setting on.

And I hate to admit it, but it’s basically bootleg DLSS Frame Generation for your living room.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

Just like PC frame generation tricks of old, your TV’s motion interpolation processor looks at two real frames from your console, guesses what should happen in between them, and inserts an artificial frame to smooth out the motion.

The moment I flipped it on in GTA 6, that nauseating camera stutter when cruising down Ocean Beach vanished. Panning around a crowded street or taking a high-speed corner suddenly felt dramatically more fluid — nowhere near 60 fps, and definitely not my desktop rig, but miles smoother than the choppy presentation.

Before the AV forums come for my head with pitchforks, let’s be completely honest about the trade-offs. There is no such thing as a free lunch in frame interpolation:.

Recent findings suggest that because your TV has to wait for the next frame before it can invent the one in the middle, motion smooth adds latency between pressing a button and seeing the result on screen. In twitchy, competitive games, that’s a death sentence.

But in a Rockstar open-world game — where character movement is already famously weighty and deliberate — I never noticed that extra latency.

Your TV’s processor is just guessing after all, and while it is a good guesser, there are some moments of weird shimmering around fast-moving objects and some boiling around on-screen elements like subtitles. Probably compounded by the fact GTA 6 is already running its own resolution scaling tech under the hood.

Standard Game Mode and VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) automatically lock out motion smoothing on many TVs. Depending on your set, you either have to turn on the dedicated low-latency Game Motion Plus mode (found on newer Samsung and LG sets) or sacrifice VRR to unlock it.

The silver lining, though, is that with this being a 30 FPS game, it’s not high enough to require VRR anyway.

If GTA 6’s 30 FPS cap is giving your eyes a workout and you want to test the dark arts yourself, don’t just blindly max out every slider.

If your TV has a low-latency interpolation option (like Samsung’s Game Motion Plus or LG’s TruMotion tweaks), use that before turning off Game Mode completely.

Set Judder Reduction to a middle ground (around 5-7 out of 10) rather than maxing it out. You want to take the harsh edge off camera pans without turning your car into a blurry smudge.

It has been revealed that this is optional based on personal taste. Test how your TV’s smoothing looks with GTA’s built-in motion blur turned off. For a lot of OLED owners, letting the TV handle the smoothing cleanly beats stacking two different blur effects on top of each other.

Do I want to play GTA 6 at native 240 FPS on my PC rig? Obviously. The second Rockstar drops the PC version, I’ll be uninstalling this hack from my brain and never looking back.

I still wouldn’t be caught dead watching a movie with motion smoothing turned on. But until PC gamers get their turn in Vice City, breaking the ultimate TV rule is the best survival trick I’ve found for making a 30 FPS masterpiece actually feel better to play.

According to recent reports, also yes, my wife has taken note of the fact that I share the same name as the male protagonist. And yes, she is side-eyeing how I treat Lucia hard.

  • Industry observers note that on Friday’s Season 24 finale of Real Time, the comedian expressed his fascination with the “giant cultural phenomenon” following GTA VI‘s multi-billion dollar opening.
  • It has been revealed that “Grand Theft Auto came out yesterday, and about a fifth of the young men in America stayed home and didn’t go to work, to play a game,” mentioned Maher in his opening monologue.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

After Grand Theft Auto VI and James Bond took over social media this week, Bill Maher has added his two cents to the discourse before going on hiatus.

Industry observers note that on Friday’s Season 24 finale of Real Time, the comedian expressed his fascination with the “giant cultural phenomenon” following GTA VI‘s multi-billion dollar opening. “No movie ever did that,” he noted.

It has been revealed that “Grand Theft Auto came out yesterday, and about a fifth of the young men in America stayed home and didn’t go to work, to play a game,” mentioned Maher in his opening monologue. “This thing has caused more workplace absences than ICE.”.

Thursday marked the release of Grand Theft Auto VI from Rockstar Games, the first GTA installment since 2013. Following a record-breaking launch, the highly-anticipated video game has already amassed $3.79B in its first 48 hours. Watch on Deadline.

Industry observers note that later in the episode, Maher mentioned, “I am intrigued by it. But again, you are criminals, and you’re doing criminal activities—not all criminal activities, and not unmotivated criminal activities. But it is something disturbing about so many people wanting to do this.

According to recent reports, “I heard … you can either choose to be a good boyfriend or a bad boyfriend,” he added. “And the guy stated, ‘Why would you choose in a video game to be a good boyfriend?’ You know, people wanna smack the hooker with the car antenna. There’s just something a little disturbing about it.”.

Pivoting to Robert Pattinson’s casting as James Bond in Denis Villeneuve’s 007, Maher praised Amazon MGM Studios for the casting choice.

“I think he’s great. I don’t understand what all this hoopla is about it,” he said. “What, is he too millennial, he’s too gay, he’s too fake? He’s great, he’s perfect … He’s 40. Perfect! You need a grown ass man to be James Bond. James Bond’s not a boy.”.

In a recent development, maher added, “And also, I would have been happy with Black James Bond, because you can be James Bond and be Black. I wouldn’t have been happy with a woman or a lesbian James Bond, that’s a different character. James Bond is a very heterosexual male, that’s too essential to not have that be a part of James Bond.”.

It has been revealed that real Time‘s Season 24 finale comes after HBO gave the show another two-season renewal earlier this year, with its Season 25 return set for Jan. 15.

iPhone Duo is getting three new features in iOS 27.3

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (661 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: 9to5mac

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • iOS 27.3 introduces next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.
  • Apple is granting iPhone Duo consumers one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.
  • According to recent reports, face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient latest option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

iOS 27.3 introduces next month and includes several exciting changes for iPhone Duo, here’s what’s new for Apple’s foldable model.

Apple is granting iPhone Duo consumers one of their biggest feature requests: face unlock is coming with iOS 27.3.

According to recent reports, face unlock isn’t a full-fledged Face ID, and it doesn’t work for features like Apple Pay, but it is a convenient latest option for unlocking your iPhone Duo just by looking at it. Per Apple:.

Recent findings suggest that use the front camera, along with a recent Touch ID or passcode authentication, to quickly unlock iPhone Duo when it’s closed. Face recognition data never leaves your device.

In a recent development, if your iPhone Duo has gone unused for 45 minutes or more, face unlock won’t work and you’ll need to authenticate with Touch ID or your passcode. But for most users, that probably just means using Touch ID first thing in the morning, then relying on face unlock the rest of the day.

According to recent reports, on a related note, you can also enable Attention Aware features in iOS 27.3. These are available whether you use the face unlock feature or not, but are limited to the outer display. Once enabled, they can automatically lower the volume of alarms and timers, keep the display from dimming, and more.

Read more: iOS 27.3 adds upcoming face unlock feature for iPhone Duo.

It has been revealed that reachability is available on other iPhone models to move onscreen content down vertically, closer to your thumb. But on iPhone Duo with iOS 27.3, Apple has a unique twist on the feature.

Instead of helping you reach content vertically, Reachability on iPhone Duo works horizontally.

If you’re using the outer screen and find that buttons or other UI elements are out of reach, you can swipe from the side to have onscreen content shift closer to your thumb.

You can always disable Reachability if you find yourself accidentally triggering it too often. But if one-handed iPhone Duo use gives you trouble, Reachability is a great new option to have.

Read more: iOS 27.3 introduces upcoming iPhone Duo feature for one-handed use.

It has been revealed that what should happen when you close your iPhone Duo’s folding screen? Apple has found that consumers have different preferences. Some want the iPhone to stay unlocked for continued use, while others prefer that it automatically locks when closed.

In iOS 27.3, Apple adds a latest setting so consumers can enable whichever behavior they prefer.

By default, iPhone Duo will work as it always has, staying unlocked after being closed. But inside Settings ⇾ Display & Brightness, iOS 27.3 provides the option of automatically locking upon being closed instead. You could achieve something similar before with Shortcuts, but now there’s a built-in setting too.

It’s not exactly a “upcoming feature,” but iPhone Duo users will also find that the system keyboard has changed in iOS 27.3. Apple tweaked the outer display keyboard to push keys closer together and make one-handed use easier.

Here’s a comparison of the old and new keyboards via Beta Profiles on X:.

iOS 27.3 beta tweaks iPhone Duo's outer display keyboard, with narrower keys and a slightly thinner, smaller font. pic.twitter.com/BDKCBZc52Z.

Read more: iOS 27.3 changes the iPhone Duo keyboard, here’s how.

Which latest iPhone Duo features in iOS 27.3 are you most excited for? Let us know in the comments.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re looking for a gift for a DIY enthusiast in your life, or if you have some big home projects to tackle over the winter, you might be looking for some new tools. If you’re looking to save money, Black Friday sales are often the lowest prices of the year on quality tools. Here are some of the best early Black Friday 2026 tool deals you can snag right now at Lowe’s.

It has been revealed that cordless power tools are a game changer for DIY projects and home maintenance because they’re compact and portable and they allow you to drive screws and bolts, drill holes, and make cuts for tasks like patching drywall, putting up shelves, or adding hardware to cabinets. Saving some money on good quality cordless tools can help you save on replacing your tools and batteries down the road too.

The DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless drill is on sale for $99, 44% off its regular price. This tool comes with a 20-volt, 2-amp-hour battery and a charger. This is the first tool I would buy if I were starting a newly introduced tool set because it allows you to drive screws as well as drill holes.

The DeWalt 20-volt MAX cordless oscillating multi-tool kit is on sale for $99, 50% off its usual price. This set comes with a 2-amp-hour battery, a charger, three starter blades, four pieces of sandpaper, a sanding attachment, and a depth guide. This tool is very handy for a home tool set because you can use it to plunge-cut drywall, trim wooden moulding, cut PVC pipe, and shape tile.

Industry observers note that the DeWalt 20-volt MAX 4.5” paddle switch angle grinder is on sale for $209, 47% off its typical price. This tool comes with a 2-amp-hour battery and a 4-amp-hour battery. You’ll need a 20-volt DeWalt charger to use it. This is a good tool for metalworking and for trimming the ends of nails and screws that poke through.

Having the right hand tools is crucial for successful DIY projects, and having the right bits and accessories saves a lot of time lost to taking extra trips to the hardware store while you’re working.

Industry observers note that the Craftsman 242-piece mechanics tool set is on sale for $99, 56% off its regular price. The set comes with a ¼-inch, a ⅜-inch, and a ½-inch drive ratchet, sockets in standard and metric sizes, a set of box wrenches, a set of driver bits, a driver handle, a set of Allen keys, and a toolbox. This is a good set to start a hand tool collection with, especially for working on vehicles or home maintenance projects like changing air filters.

The DeWalt 110-piece bit set is on sale for $29.98, 40% off its usual price. The set comes with a set of multimaterial drill bits, a set of extended shaft driver bits, a magnetic bit sheath, and several types of standard driver tips. This is a good set for most DIY projects.

The DeWalt 35-piece driver bit set is on sale for $9.98, 41% off its typical price. This set comes with driver tips in a variety of standard types and a bit sheath for driving longer screws. This is a good basic set that can be used with your driver to assemble flat-pack furniture, swap hardware on drawers and cabinets, or tighten squeaky door hinges.

The best early deals on tools right now are at Home Depot, where you can get up to 65% off on select Milwaukee tools, 50% off on DeWalt tools, and 30% off on Ryobi tools. They also have several offers for over 50% off on hand tools.

Industry observers note that home Depot and Lowe’s often compete with each other for seasonal sales, so it’s always a good idea to check both sites before buying. Right now, Home Depot has the best deals on DeWalt and Milwaukee cordless tool sets, but Lowe’s has a better deal on Craftsman hand tool sets.

The best prices of the year on tools are during the holidays in November and December. This is because of the holiday shopping push, as well as making space for fresh tools that come out in the spring. The second-best time to buy tools is in May and June during Father’s Day sales.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The best Black Friday phone deals can save you hundreds of dollars on a brand new handset, but they're not the only deals available right now. There are plenty of phone accessories that are being discounted too, but choosing between them can be quite tricky.

Lucky for you, I've spent a lot of time using different phone accessories, and know how to spot a good deal when they appear. I've already spotted a bunch of deals on things I already own, but there are also a bunch of enticing deals for things I know I'm going to need — and I'm passing on the best ones to you.

Here are the seven best Black Friday phone accessory deals I'd buy right now.

Sources indicate that screen protectors used to be the bane of my existence until they started selling kits for easy application. Now, the only time I mess up applying a screen protector is when I didn't clean the screen properly.

There are a lot of applicators out there, but I like this style from Tocol. Place the applicator on your phone before pulling the strip to expose the adhesive on the back of the screen protector. Press it down, and you can sit back and watch the air bubbles disappear.

Energizer is good for more than just batteries, and this wireless charging stand is crazy cheap for Black Friday. The 15W stand is capable of charging your phone, earbuds and an Apple Watch, with folding mechanisms that let it take up less space when you're not using it. Best Buy are also giving away three months of Apple Music and a month of Apple TV with every purchase.

Sources indicate that remember when any charger faster than 10W used to be enormous? That's no longer the case, and Anker's 45W Nano charger is easily one of my favorite compact options. Not only is it small and portable, the metal prongs fold into the charging brick for even better portability. Plus there's a boost mode that allows up to 65W charging speeds for limited periods.

Anker also sells a 47W variant with two USB-C ports, which is right now on sale for $18 and a $25 version that features a mini screen displaying your recharge progress.

Recent findings suggest that energizer also sells a magnetic power bank, which clips onto the back of compatible phones with MagSafe and other compatible connectors. Speed is limited to 15W for wireless charging and 18W wired charging — if you even use it for that. A 5,000 mAh version is also available for $12, with a slightly thinner design.

In a recent development, the Popsocket is the one phone accessory I wouldn't ever live without, and the MagSafe-compatible version is easily the most convenient. Not only does it give you a secure grip, which doubles as a phone stand, its easy to remove and replace.

That way you can swap it out for other MagSafe accessories when needed, or mix up the design whenever your mood strikes.

In a recent development, I know the pitfalls of not using a phone case all too well, and would encourage everyone to protect their phone with one. But which one do you buy? I've always been partial to Otterbox cases, on account of how much effort goes into protecting your phone.

In fact, my dad once claimed that an Otterbox kept his iPhone safe the time he foolishly decided to reverse his car over it. I don't know whether he was exaggerating or not, but it's stuck in my head ever since.

The downside is that Otterbox cases are expensive, but with $21 off that price feels a lot more reasonable.

One of the things I hate about travelling is not having all the comforts at home available. Which is especially awkward when it comes to charging my devices. Thankfully, Belkin's folding wireless charger folds up in a way that's well suited to travel.

It has been revealed that the Qi2.2 magnetic charger supports 25W wireless charging speeds, and includes a fold-out Apple Watch charger for extra convenience. It comes with built-in cooling, while also being bundled with a suitable 45W charging brick and USB-C cable, which doesn't always happen.

This Note-Taking Pebble Ring Is so Simple, and I Love It

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (898 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos.
  • According to recent reports, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity.
  • To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, pebble’s $75 ring, the Index 01, has one job: It lets you record voice memos. That seems like it would be underwhelming, and the idea was ridiculed by some of Pebble’s fans when the product was first revealed. But I’ve been wearing it for a few weeks, and folks: I love it.

According to recent reports, in this era where every tech product is trying to also be every other tech product, I appreciate the Index’s simplicity. This is a ring with no heart rate sensors or even charging pins, just a microphone, a button to activate it, and a light to let you know that it’s working. The audio is processed on your device; no need to send anything to the cloud.

To buy the Index 01 ring, you get yourself a sizing kit (either buy one for $10 or 3D print it yourself), order the ring, and pair it with the Pebble app on your phone. I use an iPhone rather than an Android, which means I can’t use certain features like setting timed reminders or connecting to Beeper, but it’s still an incredibly useful little device. The Index has no charger, since it uses a disposable battery that Pebble estimates will last about two years.

It has been revealed that the simplest way to use the Index is to wear it on your index finger (hence the name, get it?) and press the button with your thumb. Speak a quick note while holding the button in, and the ring will flash to let you know it got the message. A moment later, you’ll get a notification saying that it added (whatever you mentioned) to your “Notes to self” note.

To take this further, you can create different notes and ask the ring to add what you say to a specific note. You can also double-click the button to ask a question. The answer will appear in the notification you get on your phone or watch a moment later. (The ring does not speak to you.).

According to recent reports, all the notes you leave yourself appear as plain text in the Pebble app, fully editable. If you tap on each one, you can see a timestamp from when you left the note, and you can replay the voice recording if the transcription doesn’t make sense. (Why is there a “pencil sharp pepper” on my packing list? Ohh, that’s a pencil sharpener.) You can also add notes by typing them, which I find useful when starting a to-do list or a packing list.

Recent findings suggest that it’s incredible how useful a simple timestamped note can be. I used to do something similar with my “notes to self” chat in Signal, but the Index makes it even easier since I won’t get distracted by opening my phone. For example, I make a note on the Index whenever I take a medication, so that tomorrow morning I will be able to check whether I already took, say, a long-acting allergy pill. (You do not want to accidentally double up on those.).

Sources indicate that there’s one thing that, for years, I wished for a simple tool to help me do. It’s trivial, which makes it extra frustrating that I have not been able to find a good solution. I would simply like to note when I leave for a road trip, and when I start and end each stop. This way I can tell how long the driving took as a portion of the whole trip, and how long my stops tend to be so I can plan them better next time.

It has been revealed that you’d think this would be easy, but every existing tool drove me nuts in a different way. Stopwatches only store a single number, so I can’t break down how long each stop was—and if I miss a button press, I’m screwed. Sending myself a Signal text is probably my best option, but if I’ve just parked my car after three hours of driving, the second I pick up my phone I’m going to see all the notifications that arrived while I was on the road, and I’ll forget to actually send that text.

But this is exactly what the Index does well. I don’t even need to open my phone or look at my watch. Pressing the button with my thumb means I can do this one-handed without having a microphone always listening. (It’s also a great way to jot down the random things I think of while driving.).

The Index worked perfectly for my travel log, and I even used it for a workout after I got to my hotel room that night. I’d do 10 pushups, then tell the ring “add 10 pushups to my workout.” I’d do 20 crunches, and add that as well. I left the workout note open on my phone and could glance over and see what I had already done, since my messages got added to the note as I went.

Sources indicate that I didn’t need a workout app for any of this, or a special-purpose travel app. I can just leave myself a dang note, and the note-taking app can remember when I left the note and, if I choose, play back exactly how I mentioned it. It’s gloriously simple. Good job, Pebble.

Siri AI and select other AI features will begin having usage limits in iOS 27.3 for advanced tasks.

According to recent reports, here’s an example from the iOS 27.3 beta showing what it looks like when you hit your Siri AI daily usage limit. Per Ben in a post on X:.

I hit my Siri AI usage limit, it still works though, including complex questions pic.twitter.com/XYYNPMnSnn.

One question that Apple hasn’t made clear is what qualifies as a complex or “advanced” Siri AI request. The organization shares just two examples of something advanced:.

Suppose it gets it wrong like it does most of the time. I wonder if that still counts.

But leaker pdfu has discovered exactly the instructions Siri AI follows to determine whether a request counts as basic or advanced. In a post on X he outlines the parameters for requests deemed “advanced.”.

Siri AI will check the request against this list, and if it involves any of these, it’s deemed “advanced.”.

It would be helpful if Apple publicly documented these guidelines for owners. But perhaps after iOS 27.3 ships and usage limits are fully implemented, we’ll get more detail from the company.
