📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that every once in a while, Instagram rolls out an revision that addresses one of its users’ most longstanding requests. Today is one of those days.

As spotted by The Verge, Instagram head Adam Mosseri confirmed today that the app will finally let customers edit a Story after publishing.

This means people will be able to add stickers and drawings, fix typos or adjust text, and even change the music without having to delete the Story and publish it again, which would mean losing any views it had already received.

The catch is that users will only have 15 minutes after publishing a Story to make changes by tapping the ellipsis button at the bottom of the screen, and then selecting “Edit story.”.

Here’s Mosseri’s post announcing the news:.

A post shared by Adam Mosseri (@mosseri).

Today’s upgrade is the latest in a series of changes Instagram has made this year to address longstanding user requests.

Back in March, the app introduced the ability to reorder photos and videos in a carousel after publishing. In April, it added an option to edit comments (also within 15 minutes of posting), and in June, it began letting people manually rearrange posts on their profile grid.

More recently, Instagram also brought its free Edits video editor to the Mac, with multi-track editing, advanced color grading tools, and 4K exports.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.
  • In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue stated Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that in a new interview with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, Apple Music’s Zane Lowe discussed the early days of Apple Music Radio and revealed just how many people tune in each month. Here are the details.

Apple is rarely terribly specific about how many people use its services, including how many tune in to its radio stations.

In 2019, for instance, Eddy Cue stated Beats 1 (now Apple Music 1) had ‘tens of millions of listeners,’ but Apple has rarely provided more specific figures since.

Apple Music’s Zane Lowe, however, has now offered a more concrete figure, revealing that the service reaches over 50 million unique listeners every month:.

Industry observers note that we were never, you know, delusional enough to assume we were going to get a huge audience overnight. We’d have to build it like anyone else would have to build anything. But we’ve just got to a point in our 11 years on where we now, overall, reach over 50 million unique listeners a month, which is a really large number for us, and it’s growing exponentially and really fast.

The revelation came in a wide-ranging interview published today with Billboard’s On the Record with Kristin Robinson, where Lowe discussed Apple Music Radio’s early struggles, its approach to supporting emerging artists, and why human curation remains central to the service.

When discussing the early days at Apple Music, Lowe recalled:.

When we started the radio here, I didn’t have access or opportunity with a lot of the artists that I built relationships with from the BBC because we were unproven. And I came over here thinking, “Well, I’ve got Jimmy Iovine over here, and I’ve got Apple over here and I feel unstoppable, and who’s not going to want to come and launch this thing with us?” But it was kind of crickets… As upsetting as that was at the time, two good things came out of it. Number one, it snapped me back into the reality force field of building something from scratch. And number two, it made us focus really clearly and in a big way on new and emerging artists.

He also mentioned some of the first artists Apple Music Radio supported, including Billie Eilish with “Ocean Eyes,” Khalid with American Teen, and Bryson Tiller with his first song.

At the time, Lowe noted, these artists were just getting started, and supporting emerging talent became a defining part of Apple Music Radio’s approach, one that continues to this day:.

The really cool number is on our radio network. We played — this year alone — over 6,500 individual artists, which is not a commercial radio model. [Other radio networks’] playlists are very small, and the amount of plays is very great. Our playlist is gigantic. We play a lot of different artists, and over half of those 6,500 artists we’ve played in one year are new or emerging. So, think about 3,300 artists, roughly, getting played, who may be on their first song, their first EP, their first album…It’s proof of concept. It’s great.

Still on the subject of the early days at Apple Music, Lowe said “it was very clear [from the start] that that was very important to everybody who was responsible for bringing Apple Music to life,” adding that “serving artists and the artistic community in a way that is of most value and of most service” still drives “a lot of the decision-making” at the platform.

When the conversation turned to Apple Music’s recent rebranding, which introduced a latest logo physically created using sound waves from a composition by Fred again.., Lowe remarked he couldn’t speak to the decisions behind it, but stressed the human element and the creative process that went into it:.

We could have created that in a way that could utilize all of the tech available. We could type that into a prompt. But at the end of the day, seeing how it’s made is so much more additionally inspiring than just seeing it. It speaks to, I think, what we try to do here, which is, we love the process of what we do, and the result is a byproduct of getting to do it and loving to do it.

The problem of algorithms also came up when Lowe discussed Apple Music’s approach to music discovery, with the executive emphasizing the importance of human curation over automated recommendations:.

Well, we don’t want to say that too loudly, because someone could be like, “Wait a minute, we could cut costs here? Man, how did we not think of that!” Look, I mean, jokes aside, we’ve been incredibly fortunate, and I’ve been incredibly fortunate to take that step from the BBC into a company and to work with people that value exactly what it is you’re describing: this idea of place and this experience of sharing things with each other, and how meaningful it is when someone shares a record with you and it comes with context. It’s a gift….

Recent findings suggest that amazon’s Black Friday and Cyber Monday sale has officially started—but keeping track of the best discounts yet to land and figuring out which deals are worthwhile can be a challenge. As an alternative, you can have Alexa give you a heads-up about deals on products you already know you want to purchase, so you don’t have to spend time sorting through the noise.

Then head to the Alexa mobile app and go to More in the top left (the three horizontal lines) > Settings > Notifications > Amazon Shopping and toggle on Deal Recommendations under the Shopping Recommendations options. This ensures you’ll receive notifications for items that appear in your shopping activity.

If Alexa finds an upcoming deal on something in your Saved for Later, your Wish List, or in your Shopping Cart, you’ll receive a pop-up alert on your Echo Show display or see a yellow light ring on your Echo speaker. You can also ask, “Alexa, what are my notifications?” to hear a list of deals it has compiled thus far. You can also say "Alexa, let me know when [product name] goes on sale.".

Alexa can detect deals up to 24 hours in advance, so you can either ask it to remind you again when a deal starts or request that it buy the item when the deal goes live. Simply say, “Alexa, buy it for me,” and it’ll charge the default payment and send the item to the default delivery address on your account.

So cozy up with your blanket, raid the fridge for some snacks, and read on for three movies worth streaming on Prime Video this weekend.

I didn’t have “Nicolas Cage plays John Madden” on my 2026 bingo card, but here we are, and I’m thrilled about it, even though I don't much care for football. I care about games, and I care about Cage, and you get plenty of both here.

Director David O. Russell traces Madden’s whole arc, from his Super Bowl-winning years running the Oakland Raiders to the legendary broadcasting career that made him a household name, right up to the video game that slapped his name on millions of games for multiple consoles.

Whether you grew up quoting Madden’s broadcasts or just spent your weekends button-mashing through “Madden NFL,” this one’s a loving, larger-than-life tribute to an American original.

It has been revealed that watch "Madden" on Prime Video on Nov. 18.

It has been revealed that if your nostalgia receptors are still calibrated to the late ’90s, “I’ll Be Home for Christmas” is going to hit you like a Mack truck. This 1998 Disney comedy is pure, uncut comfort food, starring peak-era Jonathan Taylor Thomas. He plays Jake, a spoiled college kid on the west coast whose estranged dad (Gary Cole) dangles a vintage Porsche in front of him if he can just make it home to Latest York for Christmas.

Naturally, nothing goes as it should. Some classmates strand Jake out in the desert wearing a Santa suit and beard, and he has to figure out how to get home before the holiday clock runs out. Meanwhile, his girlfriend Allie (Jessica Biel) gives up waiting and accepts a cross-country ride from Jake’s rival.

Sources indicate that look, it’s not reinventing the genre, and that's fine. But JTT is genuinely charming as a selfish kid who slowly figures out what the season’s actually about. Relax and let the holiday vibes wash over you.

Watch "I'll Be Home For Christmas" on Prime Video.

Recent findings suggest that lori Petty is Rebecca Buck, aka Tank Girl, a punky blonde surviving in a post-apocalyptic 2033 where a nasty megacorporation called Water & Power is hoarding all the well, water and power. When Kesslee (Malcolm McDowell) kills her friends and burns down her life, Rebecca commandeers a tank, teams up Jet Girl (Naomi Watts) and a band of kangaroo-human mutant rebels called the Rippers, and sets out to bring the whole system down.

It's a great time to sell your soul—or take advantage of the 30-day free trial—and there's a lot more to your membership than just deals and free shipping.

According to recent reports, the standard Prime membership costs $14.99 per month or $139 per year, but there are other tiers that some people might qualify for. For example, the Amazon Prime for Young Adults program allows young adults between the ages of 18 and 24 to get all of the Prime perks for half the cost—$7.49 per month or $69 annually.

Sources indicate that I'll be the first to admit I didn't know all of the benefits that Amazon Prime offers to its members. There are a lot more perks than people think. Here are the most impressive ones (and check out the full list):.

Fast free shipping on millions of items: Depending on where you live, shipping can take one or two days, and some even come on the same day for orders of $25 or more in most areas—and it’s always free (if being shipped by the Amazon store).

Select pre-ordered items can be delivered on their release date for free (for most areas).

The option to have items delivered inside your garage with a smart garage device (depending on where you live) for $1.99 per order, or for free if you combine it with Amazon Day delivery.

Earn rewards for future purchases when you select free no-rush shipping.

The option to have all your weekly orders delivered on a specific day, to reduce waste from boxes.

Amazon Prime Visa card: Cardholders get 5% back on Amazon, Whole Foods, Chase Travel, and other purchases. Prime members who use this card extensively can earn rewards that offset the cost of membership.

Sources indicate that A Grubhub+ and Uber Eats membership, normally $9.99 per month, which gets you free delivery on eligible orders, lower service fees, exclusive deals, and other perks as long as you remain a Prime Member (it used to be only for a year). The Uber Eats membership gets you free delivery on eligible restaurants of $25 or more.

It has been revealed that sharing with family or friends: Amazon Family is the existing program for sharing Prime benefits, and it allows you to add separate profiles for one other adult who lives in the same household as the primary account holder, up to four teens, and up to four child accounts. This grants access to all the standard benefits, such as free delivery, Prime Video with ads, Prime Reading, third-party benefits like Grubhub, and access to audiobooks, e-books, certain games, and Amazon Music.

Industry observers note that amazon Health: Prime owners get One Medical access for an additional $9 per month or $99 per year. Through your devices, you’ll have 24/7 access to on-demand virtual care, plus real-life access to primary care offices in a number of U.S. cities. It accepts most major health insurance prepares, too.

Amazon Pharmacy: Access to free two-day delivery and other savings on medications.

Prime Video: Prime includes unlimited streaming of movies, TV shows, and Amazon Originals with ads, which normally costs $9 per month.

Amazon Music Prime: Access to Amazon's Spotify-esque music streaming service (not to be confused with Amazon's other music streaming subscriptions).

Amazon Luna: A cloud gaming platform that offers latest free games every month, free downloadable PC games, content, a monthly Twitch channel subscription, and a free channel subscription on Twitch each month for Prime Members.

Amazon Photos: Unlimited photo storage plus 5 GBs for videos and other files (which extends to members of your Family Vault).

Prime Reading: Free access to a rotating selection of e-books and magazines for Kindle or Fire tablets and Kindle apps.

Amazon's First Reads: You get up to two free e-books every month from a curated list of books handpicked by editors.

#39648. These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1508 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

These 14 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1508 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov.
  • Industry observers note that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program.
  • Sources indicate that the iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the manufacturer's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, apple has been beta testing iOS 27.3 since Nov. 3. While this enhancement isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially debuts the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Industry observers note that technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger problems. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

Sources indicate that the iPhone Duo is Apple's first foldable smartphone, but also the manufacturer's first phone since the iPhone SE 3 to ship with Touch ID. While it works well enough for unlocking your iPhone, it's still an adjustment for those of us used to Face ID. With iOS 27.3, Apple is now testing face unlock for the Duo—not Face ID, mind you. The Duo's front camera doesn't have the tech required to power Face ID or its secure protocols. Instead, this feature simply unlocks your iPhone Duo with a face scan. In addition, your Duo will still require Touch ID for Apple Pay and passwords, or after 45 minutes of inactivity. You can read more about this upcoming feature here.

In a recent development, iOS 27.3 also comes with a upcoming setting that lets you lock your iPhone Duo by closing it—as you would expect from, say, a laptop—or, dare I say, a flip phone? At the moment, closing the Duo seamlessly transitions what's on the significant screen to the smaller display, and you have to press the side button to lock the phone.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a latest set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the organization is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,.

It has been revealed that the organization generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company claims Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

According to recent reports, despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

In a recent development, for example, you could ask Siri AI to help you proposal a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These latest actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Industry observers note that apple started testing its newly introduced Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

It has been revealed that continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training strategy. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

It has been revealed that apple is also testing a latest Siri AI feature in Safari, that gives the bot access to entire webpages, including the parts of the site that aren't on-screen. Say you want to know all the gluten-free options on a menu on a restaurant's website, but only a portion of the site is actually in view. You could ask Siri to read you the gluten-free options, and it would pull from the whole page, even though you can only see part of it.

According to recent reports, vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Industry observers note that another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Industry observers note that apple is also testing newly introduced StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability at the moment works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Sources indicate that apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

It has been revealed that if you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

It has been revealed that if you watch videos in Apple Podcasts, you can find them in more sources than the Podcasts app. With the new updates, you'll find these videos on Apple TV 4K, select smart TVs, your iPhone, iPad, Mac, and even in CarPlay. (Please don't watch video podcasts while driving.).

A Tesla Cybercab on display at the Auto Zürich show in Zurich in November 2026.

It has been revealed that tesla has started offering rides in its Cybercab in Dallas, the second city after Austin for the two-seater with no steering wheel or pedals. Tesla already runs Model Y robotaxis in Dallas and prepares to start delivering Cybercabs to private buyers in Texas in December.

Tesla’s Cybercab, its two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, is now giving rides in Dallas, InsideEVs reported. “Cybercab has arrived in your city,” Tesla’s Robotaxi account posted on X on Thursday.

Industry observers note that dallas is the second city to get the Cybercab, after it began giving rides in Austin in September. Tesla already runs driverless Model Y robotaxis in Dallas. Riders book both in the Tesla Robotaxi app.

It has been revealed that tesla’s robotaxis also run in Houston, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Tampa, Orlando and Miami, mostly with the Model Y. It has focused on Texas and Florida, where the rules are looser than in states like California.

The US road safety agency, NHTSA, is looking into how Tesla decided a car with no wheel or pedals meets US safety rules. Unlike Amazon’s Zoox, Tesla did not ask for an exemption. NHTSA is also reviewing claims that Tesla robotaxis, including Cybercabs, sped in school zones.

Tesla is also starting to sell the Cybercab to some customers for $29,990. Owners must pay a $299 monthly fee, or the car will not run. The first cars should reach buyers in Texas in December.

To build more of them, Tesla intends to wind down Cybertruck output at its Texas plant around mid-2027.

Despite having a one-inch layer of micro coils, the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper is far plusher than you’d think. I would describe the surface as medium-soft with just the right amount of sinkage for a comfortable night's sleep on your side and back. Special attention has been made to those with back pain, with zoned lumbar support cradling the spine and relieving pressure on sore joints. The foam padding means it sleeps warmer than the latex Saatva topper I've tested, but the recycled steel micro-coil layer offsets most of that stuffiness. Why you can trust Tom's Guide Our writers and editors spend hours analyzing and reviewing products, services, and apps to help find what's best for you. Find out more about how we test, analyze, and rate.

Alongside some of the best mattresses from Saatva, the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper is the third mattress topper I've recently tested from this luxury sleep brand — so I thought I knew what to expect.I expected a micro-coil topper to be comfortable but firm like the best hybrid mattresses I've tested. After all, Saatva advertises it as a pressure-relieving topper with “firmer support.”.

Imagine my surprise when I realized that the Micro-Coil Mattress Topper is the softest of the three toppers I've tested from Saatva.

Type: Foam + Micro coilsDepth: 3"Cover: CottonCorner straps: YesTrial period: 45 nightsWarranty: 1-year warrantyStarting MSRP: from $235 at Saatva.

It has been revealed that the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has a soft, contouring surface with an enough give around the shoulders and hips to make side sleeping the most comfortable position, with back sleeping a close second. Firmness is subjective, but I personally wouldn't recommend the Micro-Coil to stomach sleepers, especially those who weigh more than me (180 lbs). For a firmer Saatva topper, I'd go for the Saatva Graphite Mattress Topper.

As a back and stomach sleeper, the topper is almost too soft for my liking, but not enough to prevent a deep night’s sleep. It's a great option for anyone looking to soften up a firm mattress without compromising back support (zoned support from the coils and foam maintain healthy spinal alignment, which is key for back pain).Temperature-wise, I did feel some stuffiness from the foam layer (more so than I did sleeping on the naturally cooling Saatva Natural Latex topper). But as long as I slept in lightweight pyjamas and breathable bedding, I was able to comfortably sleep through the night. If I wore anything heavier, I woke up to some warmth.

According to recent reports, ultimately, the Saatva Micro-Coil Topper is a great choice for anyone looking to soften up a too-firm mattress or prolong the life of a bed that's losing its support. Don't let the micro-coil layer fool you, it's softer than advertised. But if you're a side or back sleeper looking to sample the luxury of the best Saatva mattresses as a fraction of the cost, I highly recommend it.

The Saatva Black Friday deals are in full swing, but don't expect to see the Micro-Coil Mattress Topper on sale — accessories are never discounted, unless as part of a bundle deal. However, don't write off buying this topper just yet. At $315 for a queen, it is a premium price. However, when compared to a the Saatva Classic mattresses, which is down to $1,804 in the Saatva mattress sales, $315 doesn't seem so steep — even for just a topper. If you want to buy a luxury mattress topper at a lower price, or even buy an entire new bed for around the same cost, it's worth bookmarking our Black Friday mattress deals page, where we're tracking the best sales of the holiday season.

But for now, here are the regular prices of every Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper size:.

Get instant access to breaking news, the hottest reviews, great deals and helpful tips.

According to recent reports, micro coils are the newest innovation for toppers so they’re often priced higher than expected. Considering the pricing of Saatva’s other mattress toppers, $315 for a queen Micro-Coil Mattress Topper seems about right for the brand. The topper is shipped for free and comes with a six-month sleep trial and one-year warrantym which is considered pretty a short warranty period for the luxury topper market.

Recent findings suggest that the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has three different layers. The top layer is a cotton cover with Guardin botanical antimicrobial treatment. It prevents the growth of bacteria, mildew, and mold, which is helpful considering the cover is not removeable (and thus not washable).

Recent findings suggest that in the centre of the mattress topper is a one-inch layer of recycled steel micro-coils. They’ve been reinforced along the edges of the topper and in the center third to provide support for your hips and lower back. On either side of the micro-coil layer is gel-infused comfort foam with CertiPUR-US certification for enhanced temperature control.

Recent findings suggest that four straps are placed on the corners to keep the topper in place. Though I ordered a king topper, it did not fully cover my king-sized mattress, exposing about an inch or two on either side of the topper. (This has been the case for all of the Saatva toppers I've tested, which makes me wonder if my actual mattress is larger than I thought).

Sources indicate that my biggest concern about this mattress’ design might be the durability. Foam breaks down faster than natural latex and there is only an inch between your body and the micro coil layer. While I didn’t notice any durability problems during testing, the plusher, soft surface of the topper indicates a softer foam that may not last as long as a firmer foam, especially if you sleep in the same spot night after night.

After a week of testing the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper, here’s what I can share about the ease of set up, comfort, and temperature regulation.

According to recent reports, the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper arrived vacuum sealed and tightly rolled into a ball. Because of the micro-coils, I had to unfurl the topper by hand and place it in a flat position on my mattress. After putting the straps into place so the topper wouldn’t move, I noticed that it didn’t completely cover my king-size mattress. There was about an inch or two of the mattress visible on either side of the topper.

It has been revealed that the topper had a lot of creases and bunching because it appears to have unnecessary, extra fabric. By the time I slept on the topper at night, I could not feel the fabric through my sheets.

The off-gassing of the topper’s foams were noticeable as soon as I removed the packaging, and a week later, I can still smell it.

For a mattress topper with a layer of micro coils, I expected it to be firm and supportive. That’s how Saatva advertises it, but that’s not exactly what I experienced.

The Micro-Coil Mattress Topper has a plush, soft surface — I rate it as 5/10 on the mattress firmness scale, placing it as medium-plush. My shoulders and hips sunk in enough to allow for deep pressure relief when on my side and felt comfortably supportive when on my back. As a back and stomach sleeper who prefers a firmer mattress feel, the topper was slightly too soft for my preferences. However, the cushioning and cradling nature of the surface would appeal to most sleepers.

According to recent reports, stomach sleepers will need something firmer, like the Saatva Graphite Mattress Topper, especially those weighing over 180lbs. Comfort-wise, I’d recommend the Micro-Coil Mattress Topper to those who need to soften a firm mattress.

Thanks largely to its recycled steel coils, the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper does a decent job with temperature regulation. However, I wouldn’t suggest it for very hot sleepers.

Industry observers note that I tested this topper during a particularly cold week in Texas in November when the temperature inside my home was between 64-69 degrees at night. Because it was so cold in the evenings, I’d sometimes fall asleep with a sweatshirt and sweatpants. When that happened, I would wake up slightly warm — but not sweating and not hot. I’d then take off my socks or change into lighter pyjamas and be fine the rest of the night.

The best mattress toppers will provide a comfortable sleep feel, regardless of the temperature of your bedroom. If you like the sound of the Micro-coil, I’d suggest light sleepwear and using breathable sheets.

Whether you overheat easily or not, I’d suggest ordering this topper in the summer and utilize the 180-night sleep trial to make sure it’s a good fit for you.

Rather than separate the topper reviews, Saatva mixed them all together. This means the 4.7 out of 5-star rating from over 305 reviews is a score related to all Saatva’s toppers – and is not accurate for the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper.

You can search the topper reviews by keyword and star rating. I typed in “micro coil” and only six reviews popped up. There could be more by other buyers who didn’t mention the term “micro-coil” in their reviews.

Sources indicate that five of the six reviews praised the topper for its soft, contouring feel and how it improved their sleep by making their mattress more comfortable and/or its ability to relieve their pain. One reviewer mentioned returning the micro-coil mattress because it made them very hot at night.

✅You sleep on your side: Your shoulders and hips will sink in the right amount to allow for a comfortable night’s sleep on your side.

✅ You have a mattress that’s too firm: If your mattress is so firm that it’s causing you aches and pains, go for the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper as it’ll provide the right amount of softening to your bed.

✅You have back or joint pain: The zoned lumbar support has been designed to support the spine and reduce pressure in the lumbar region.

❌ You sleep on your stomach: Those who have smaller bodies (180-lbs. and below) could potentially sleep on your stomach on this mattress. However, for most, it won’t offer the firm support you’d need for a night of stomach sleeping.

Sources indicate that ❌ You sleep very hot: The comfort foam layer feels a little stuffy, even with the inclusion of breathable steel coils. For very hot sleepers, I recommend the Saatva Natural Latex Topper instead, which is naturally cooling.

❌ You want a washable, removable cover: You can only spot clean the exterior of this topper as the cover can’t be removed and washed.

It has been revealed that this copper-infused memory foam topper is cover free, and our reviewers found that it kept them cool at night. Its 7-zone surface technology has differing firmness levels along seven different areas of the body for superb zoned support. Read more in our Molecule CopperWELL Mattress Topper.

According to recent reports, enjoy a superbly cool night’s sleep on the Helix GlacioTex Premium Mattress Topper, a 3.75" thick topper that comes in two different firmness options. Like the Saatva Micro-Coil Mattress Topper, it has a layer of coils that aid in breathability. However, the GlacioTex cover probably does a better job to keep you from sweating or overheating at night.

Sources indicate that if you love the Saatva brand and prefer something a bit more supportive, consider the Saatva Natural Latex Mattress Topper. It’s great for combination sleepers or couples with different sleep styles. The natural latex materials promote a cooler night’s sleep, especially for those who sleep hot. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Meta employees have expressed concerns about what appear to be major privacy breaches when using Muse, at the moment the second most popular free iPhone app in the App Store with over 10 million downloads.

This includes again accessing end-to-end encrypted messaging without permission, and sharing what may be the bank balances of another Muse user ….

Siri AI was not the only AI app to launch back in September; Meta’s Muse AI app was introduced the same month, with the tech giant describing it as “your personal AI agent that gets things done across every part of life.”.

According to recent reports, muse initially rolled out as an iPhone app, with Mac and iPad apps following shortly afterwards. It immediately moved to the top of the US App Store charts, overtaking ChatGPT. It quickly exceeded 5 million downloads following a major advertising push by Meta, and that number has since doubled.

Recent findings suggest that it wasn’t long before major privacy concerns were raised. Tech writer Jason Aten reported that the Mac app accessed his messages despite him explicitly refusing permission. The app then lied to him about how it had achieved this. Meta described this as a bug.

Security researcher Patrick Wardle also discovered a zero-day vulnerability that could allow an attacker to hijack dictated prompts, directing them instead to their own server.

I said at the time that I would absolutely not be one of the millions of people using the app, and the wisdom of that decision has now been underlined by a fresh report.

Reuters now reports Meta employees discussing further breaches. This includes another example of accessing encrypted messages without permission.

An employee using Muse on her personal phone reported it had surprised her with a reminder to respond to a message from her sister on Signal, an end-to-end encrypted messaging service popular with privacy advocates that competes with Meta’s WhatsApp.

Industry observers note that “This seems like an extreme privacy violation. I definitely did not grant it access to other apps, or recall being asked about this,” the employee stated in her post.

In a recent development, the report says this appears to have been done by capturing push notifications. However, this was what the app claimed had happened in the earlier case, and it turned out not to be true. The AI Now Institute was able to replicate the problem of Muse accessing Signal messages without permission.

Another employee reported receiving unsolicited bank balances that they say appeared to be those of another Muse user.

Muse had randomly added an extra message to its regular chats about fishing-related weather and tide information, saying: “BTW, two bank updates, your Capital One balance is $2722.58, your Charles Schwab balance is $5899.57.”.

“I have never shared my bank account with Muse and never discussed any banking topic with Muse. I’m afraid it’s sending other’s bank info to me,” the staffer wrote in his post.

It has been revealed that meta told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents” and suggested that the bank balances may have been AI hallucinations rather than leaked information. Enhancement: Meta has now told us that the balances were definitely hallucinations.

"AI Agent" = Malware. There are an expanding number of "I told it not to do that" cases.

In a recent development, the instructions (prompt) you give the agent are a tiny fraction of the total prompt context the agent uses, and Meta/Grok/etc. is not going to let you see that context. Agents harvesting your data (ex. see full disk access) and sending it to the mothership is just another revenue/training stream. Even if you are paying you are still the product.

Recent findings suggest that meta has taken issue with the messaging claims. It says that access to either notifications or messaging must be explicitly granted.

Sources indicate that with Android, people have the option to grant apps notification access, which allows apps to see notifications as they’re received. This is something users need to opt in to and is not specific to Muse. With Mac, to allow Muse to work on your behalf, you not only need to click allow for accessibility and screen recording, but after that it takes you to a settings screen where you once again need to confirm and turn this on.

The company also implies that the experience of employees may relate to internal versions of Muse.

Employees have access to different versions of Muse than the public, so they’re often reviewing features, functionality, and behavior not available elsewhere.

I can only repeat my previous take on Muse: Nope.

StepSecurity’s graphic announcing its $20M Series A.

StepSecurity, a Seattle-area startup founded by two former Microsoft engineers, has raised a $20M Series A led by Elephant. It protects developers’ laptops, code repositories, package downloads and build pipelines from attackers who plant malicious code in open-source software.

According to recent reports, stepSecurity, a Seattle-area security startup, has raised a $20M Series A led by Elephant, GeekWire reported. Runtime Ventures, Inner Loop Capital and SaaS Ventures also put in money, taking its total to $23M.

Recent findings suggest that the tech giant guards the places where software gets built, from developers’ laptops to the systems that test and ship code. Hackers now often hide bad code in free, open-source software. Once it runs, it can steal passwords and keys.

According to recent reports, “A supply chain attack used to take a skilled team. Now one person can vibe code it,” CEO Varun Sharma wrote in a blog post.

According to recent reports, the round landed in a busy week. On 17 November, hackers posted two poisoned versions of agent-framework, Microsoft’s Python toolkit for AI agents, which gets nearly 200,000 downloads a month. StepSecurity was among the firms that spotted the code, which stole passwords and keys, BleepingComputer reported.

According to recent reports, tools for coders have been behind other substantial hacks. Binance says its $6.3B hack started with a fake job interview and a tampered developer tool. Last month, a tampered Claude Code extension reached up to 5,000 Cursor users.

Sharma spent about 15 years at Microsoft. Co-founder Ashish Kurmi also worked there before leading security at Uber and Plaid. They started StepSecurity in 2021 after living through the SolarWinds and Codecov attacks.

In a recent development, more than 20,000 open-source projects use its free tool, Harden-Runner. Its researchers also helped track the ChainDrop npm worm in August. StepSecurity notes its yearly revenue grew fivefold in both 2024 and 2025, but gave no figures.

Next, it plans to guard the sandboxes where AI agents run code. Worms such as Miasma already target AI coding tools. Rivals are growing too: Belgium’s Aikido became a $1B unicorn in January.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that in light of growing pushback from owners who want more control over how AI is integrated into their apps (if at all), Canva is introducing upcoming settings that let them hide generative AI features and see less AI-generated content. Here are the details.

Canva today confirmed latest controls that will let Free and Pro owners choose whether to see generative AI features across the app, as well as how much AI-generated content appears in search results and in recommendations for templates and design elements.

The organization notes that both controls are available at no additional cost and can be turned on or off at any time.

According to Canva, “the future of creativity isn’t a choice between AI and no AI.” For this reason, it is introducing the following controls:.

The manufacturer says that, while it knows that there is an ongoing debate between owners with opposing views on whether AI has a place in creative work, it thinks “both views are valid”:.

“It’s not our place to tell anyone how to create, so today we’re launching two new controls that put that decision firmly with our community […].”.

Importantly, the company noted that select features that use AI without generating fresh content will remain available even when generative AI features are turned off:.

In a recent development, “Some of Canva’s everyday editing tools use AI to make simple tasks faster, without generating anything new. Background Remover, one of Canva’s most popular tools, lifts a subject cleanly out of a photo in a single click, and Magic Grab lets creators select an object in an image and move it somewhere else in the design. Both remain available when the generative AI switch is off, because they work only with what’s already in a design.”.

Canva added that these tools also won’t add an AI label to a design’s metadata, since that label is reserved for AI-generated content.

As for the company’s design content library, Canva said that while “a small portion of the library is AI-generated content made by Canva, including some abstract backgrounds and illustrated graphics,” its community has told it “they want an easier way to find design assets made by real people, so the content control reduces the number of AI-generated templates and elements that appear in search results and recommendations.”.

With today’s announcement, Canva is essentially expanding on the AI permissions already available to administrators of Business, Enterprise, Teams, and Education accounts, which let organizations control how their teams use AI.

Industry News: Clojure will affect the way you think about programming (2017)

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1239 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Thegreenplace

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • I sometimes get asked for recommendations of what programming language to "learn next".
  • In this post I want to explain why I think Clojure is a terrific language for this task.
  • Sources indicate that first and foremost, Clojure belongs to the Lisp family of languages, like Common Lisp, Scheme and Racket.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

I sometimes get asked for recommendations of what programming language to "learn next". It's great that folks appreciate the fact that being exposed to several sufficiently different programming languages is an notable step on the path to programming enlightenment. But it's also true that, given limited free time, the choice of which languages to learn is important. As the famous quote by Alan Perlis claims:.

In this post I want to explain why I think Clojure is a terrific language for this task. Whatever your background, it's almost guaranteed to affect the way you think about programming. It's a fairly new language (from 2007) that did a good job of collecting insights and paradigms from many existing languages and organizing them into a coherent whole. It's chock-full of great ideas. In other words, the perfect language to expand your brain.

Sources indicate that first and foremost, Clojure belongs to the Lisp family of languages, like Common Lisp, Scheme and Racket. Lisp is one of the oldest and still most key families of programming languages to be familiar with. Being a Lisp in this case means several things:.

Importantly, Clojure is a very modern Lisp, with tons of libraries for tasks common in our day and age. It also builds upon notable recent research in data structures, such as efficient persistent vectors, that only appeared in the 1990s or later. I've been dabbling with various Lisps for almost 15 years, and Clojure is the first Lisp I'd consider using in production.

I want the stress the importance of full Lisp-style macros once again. Lisp's (and Clojure's) uniform syntax and macros force us to think about the Meta-circular abstraction - there's just no way around it! We have to think of our code as data, and this has profound implications. Back in 2005, when I was still a programming neophyte, I faced a performance challenge for a data-decoding program I was hacking on in Perl. Having learned some Lisp, I had the insight of generating and evaluating new Perl code on the fly, which turned out to be key to the success of that program. I'm confident I could not have come up with that solution back then without being aware of the "Lisp way".

The designers of Clojure are extremely pragmatic, building upon decades of industry experience. I strongly recommend watching some YouTube videos of talks by leading Clojure developers. In particular, watch a few of the more popular talks by Rich Hickey - Clojure's original designer. The Alan Perlis quote mentioned above may be his most popular, but there's another I find at least as insightful:.

There's a certain quality in programmers I believe we can all recognize. It can only come from real, hard-won experience of building systems for many years and pondering about how to build such systems more effectively next time. Rich Hickey certainly belongs to this quality category - his talks are very insightful, and this philosophy reigns in the design and implementation of Clojure, as well as its (friendly and vibrant) community.

Sources indicate that applications that process and extract useful bits of information from large datasets all look alike in many programming languages, at least to some extent. What we really want in many cases is SQL-like primitives built into our languages, but this is often challenging (.NET's LINQ is one example of a successful approach).

Clojure combines pervasive sequence protocols with persistent data structures and laziness to make this kind of task natural, using only built-in tools. Here's a realistic example of a function taken from the Clojure Applied book:.

All the functions used here are built-ins, including the ->> macro. This code reads like SQL and it's efficient too. In fact, it can be made somewhat more efficient and even seamlessly parallelized using Reducers and Transducers.

The clojure.spec library provides a degree of type-safety for nested data structures. If you've ever written comments like "this maps strings to lists, where each list element is a map of ...", clojure.spec makes it more formal and verifiable. This is very useful when working with data, and is another example of where Clojure's pragmatism shines; the language is dynamic in its core, but when you need static checking - it's there, optionally (core.typed is another option for a more statically typed flavor).

Sources indicate that historically, Lisp programmers weren't the biggest proponents of OOP. This doesn't mean that OOP has absolutely no value in Lisp-y languages, however. Common Lisp has had CLOS for decades, and Clojure also comes with an array of OO-like features.

Recent findings suggest that that remarked, Clojure's flavor of OOP is particularly powerful and tends to discourage bad practices. Clojure uses "protocols", which are a kind of interfaces, and encourages thinking in terms of protocols rather than in terms of classes with inheritance hierarchies, sort of like Go. Add to that an ability to do true multiple dispatch and you have a powerful modeling tool at your fingertips.

Industry observers note that it wouldn't be a real language of the 2000s without powerful support for concurrency and parallelism right at the core. Clojure supports this in many ways, which are interleaved.

According to recent reports, first, it's a functional language with persistent data structures. Persistent data structures are effectively immutable, which makes them very attractive in a multi-threaded context. Clojure has a great implementation of persistent data structures even for things like vectors (which are quite challenging to implement in an efficient manner). This is a bigger deal than may originally appear. Pure functions are often great in theory but fail in practice due to too much copying of non-trivial data structures; Clojure's elegant usage of persistent data structures solves this problem, making pure functions efficient and thus much more applicable to a wide array of problems.

Second, Clojure doesn't lock itself in the closet of purism and does support lower-level primitives for concurrency and mutation, where needed. Atoms are built-in mutable state units with atomic updates. Refs and transactions go further, implementing STM.

Industry observers note that third, Clojure comes with a bunch of concurrency tools built in. Promises, futures and threads leverage the underlying JVM's threading utilities.

Finally, Clojure has a pretty good implementation of Go's CSP in the core.async module. It provides two useful things:.

Finally, it's vital to mention that Clojure is far from being an academic exercise. It's used in production by several companies, and has strong roots in the massive Java ecosystem. Clojure's interoperability with Java is seamless - Java code can be called from Clojure with no special provisions, and all core Clojure entities are Java objects deep under the hood.

Sources indicate that on the client side, Clojurescript has been gaining traction recently as another language-compiled-to-JS option. It brings the elegance of Clojure to client-side programming, among with some unique features like core.async for callback-free concurrency.

This doesn't mean that you should only consider Clojure as a fit for your next project. On the contrary, I recommend learning if even if there's little chance of using it in production any time soon. In fact, this was exactly my situation, Clojure is a great language to expand your programming horizons; who knows, maybe in the future you'll find it useful for some real work. If you do, great! If you don't, learning it will positively affect how you use other programming languages.

Recent findings suggest that in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Sources indicate that in advanced semiconductor manufacturing, small defects can have a large effect on yield. Thin film deposition tools must stay stable and qualified. Process drift must be caught early. When a defect does appear, engineers need to know where it came from and how it affects device performance. This webinar demonstrates how in-line inspection and offline characterization combine into one workflow, from tool monitoring to root-cause analysis.

Recent findings suggest that in the first half, Dr. Bitan Chakraborty from Intel, explains how surface scan metrology fits into station monitors for thin film tools. The session shows how baseline signatures and real-time monitoring reveal hardware wear, particle generation, and process drift before they reach production wafers. It then moves to in-line scans on patterned wafers. These scans expose layer-level defects and show how they form and spread through multi-layer device stacks. Linking this defect data to electrical test results helps teams find root causes and focus their yield improvement work.

In the second half, Dr. Jacob Petersen from Evident Scientific, addresses a common question: what happens after an in-line tool flags a problem? In-line tools are fast, but they cannot always provide the details needed for a firm conclusion. Offline 3D optical profilometry fills that gap by combining three complementary inspection techniques in a single system. It delivers dimensional measurements and helps determine whether a defect lies within the sample or comes from foreign material. The session covers how several optical techniques support inspection from bare silicon to fully packaged chips. It also highlights how automation enables fast measurement of features down to the sub-nanometer scale with minimal operator handling.

Weak sales of the OLED iPad Pro are also believed to have influenced the decision.

The report suggests that incoming CEO John Ternus has been reviewing the commercial viability of upgrading more products to OLED. As further evidence, the report says Apple has sent quotation requests to LCD suppliers for an iMac screen to be launched in around 2029.

#39633. Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1514 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Valkey ↗ Open Full Page

Valkey kills the skiplist, cuts sorted set overhead by up to 43%

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1514 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Valkey

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A sorted set can spend more memory describing how its elements are ordered than storing the elements themselves.
  • In Valkey 9.2 that changes: the skiplist is replaced by a high-fanout B+ tree variant called fbtree.
  • fbtree combines the high fanout and contiguous storage of a conventional B+ tree with several optimizations designed for Valkey's workload and memory allocator, including feature-based lookups, SIMD searches, linked leaves, and fast paths for sequential inserts and pops.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A sorted set can spend more memory describing how its elements are ordered than storing the elements themselves.

In Valkey 9.2 that changes: the skiplist is replaced by a high-fanout B+ tree variant called fbtree.

fbtree combines the high fanout and contiguous storage of a conventional B+ tree with several optimizations designed for Valkey's workload and memory allocator, including feature-based lookups, SIMD searches, linked leaves, and fast paths for sequential inserts and pops. In a 5-million-member test, it reduced per-member memory overhead by 36–43%, saving up to 109 MB.

Let's take a look at why this change happened and how it works.

Large sorted sets that exceed the listpack threshold are backed by a skiplist paired with a hashtable (smaller sorted sets use a compact listpack representation that stores elements sequentially in contiguous memory). The hashtable gives O(1) lookups by member, while the skiplist gives O(log n) ordered lookups by rank or score. That pairing is architecturally simple, but the skiplist carries a significant memory cost. It stores exactly one element per node, scattered across memory as separate allocations connected by pointers.

Valkey's skiplist pays for this in raw memory. Every node carries a backward pointer (8B), plus an average of 1.33 levels of forward pointers and span values, since skiplists are probabilistic (each node has a 25% chance of gaining another level). Each level costs 8B for the pointer plus 8B for the span value, giving around 29B of pointer and span overhead per node. Add the 8B score, and the total reaches roughly 37B per node before accounting for the member string.

Modern CPUs use a hierarchy of hardware caches (L1, L2, and L3) to keep frequently accessed data close to the processor. These caches are much smaller and faster than main memory (RAM), so when the CPU cannot find the data it needs in its cache, it must fetch it from a slower level of the memory hierarchy. As a rough illustration, an L1 cache hit can take about 1 ns, while a DRAM access can take around 100 ns. A dependent memory access can leave the core waiting; actual latency and how much work can be hidden vary by system and workload 1.

According to recent reports, each node in the skiplist is a separate allocation, potentially scattered wherever the heap happened to place it, so following the structure can require repeatedly fetching data from unrelated memory locations. Because each step can determine where the next step goes, these fetches are dependent, resulting in more round trips through the memory hierarchy. A 2025 study of concurrent in-memory indexes found that, on its tested workloads, traditional skiplists experienced roughly 2.4–4.8× more cache misses than a comparable B-tree, with 2–8× lower throughput 2 (testing different data structure implementations, not Valkey).

Sources indicate that A B+ tree keeps entries sorted in fixed-size nodes: leaf nodes hold the entries, or pointers to them, and inner nodes hold just enough routing data to pick which child to descend into. Packing many entries into each node addresses both problems above: far less per-member pointer overhead, and far fewer dependent fetches per lookup.

It has been revealed that fbtree, short for Feature B+ Tree, uses a 61-way fanout: each node can hold up to 61 entries or child pointers. Leaf and inner nodes are sized to fit jemalloc allocation classes without wasting space on 64-bit builds; on supported 32-bit builds, innerNode is rounded up to the 1280-byte class.

According to recent reports, A 512-byte leaf holds up to 61 value pointers, so 61 members share one node instead of each getting its own. Instead of storing the score and member separately, fbtree stores them together as a single packed value: the normalized 8-byte score followed by the member bytes. This keeps the data needed for comparisons together and removes another level of pointer indirection.

It has been revealed that the skiplist's 25%-per-level rule gives it an effective branching factor of about 4, while fbtree's fanout is 61. Both structures retain O(log n) search complexity, but the B+ tree has substantially fewer levels to traverse and therefore fewer opportunities for expensive memory fetches.

Industry observers note that A modern CPU can also fetch several adjacent cache lines efficiently when the data is laid out contiguously, thanks in part to the way memory is accessed and to hardware prefetching 1. Therefore a B+ tree node that spans a few cache lines can be read efficiently as the CPU scans its contents.

On top of that structure, fbtree adds optimizations aimed at specific operations.

Sources indicate that in a B+ tree keyed by variable-length strings, such as sorted set members, picking a child means comparing the lookup against each child’s anchor, the largest member in that child, and reading those strings costs memory fetches. fbtree's inner nodes store each anchor along with a small four-byte "feature." Because the anchors often share a common prefix, fbtree stores that shared prefix separately and uses the four feature bytes to distinguish the children. The implementation can then compare those features in parallel using SIMD, often identifying the correct child before fetching the child node itself. If the features uniquely identify a child, the search can descend immediately; otherwise, they still narrow the range that needs a full binary search.

Range commands such as ZRANGE walk the set in order. fbtree links its leaf nodes in a doubly-linked list, so a scan can move from leaf to leaf without climbing back up the tree. The skiplist requests an item, waits to receive it, and only knows the next item to fetch when it's received the first. The B+ tree can work on up to 61 items in parallel, and while it works on those it can fetch the next leaf node with the next 61 items.

Commands such as ZPOPMIN work at the ends of the set. fbtree caches its leftmost and rightmost leaves, so finding them is O(1), as in a skiplist, instead of O(log n). This keeps pop and append operations at parity rather than regressing.

Range deletions remove a contiguous run of members, and fbtree handles them without rebuilding the surrounding structure.

Sources indicate that the change is internal: sorted set commands and their behavior remain unchanged. The one visible difference is that OBJECT ENCODING returns btree instead of skiplist for a large sorted set. If you have monitoring, tests, or tooling that checks for the literal string skiplist, that's one place to enhancement. Small sorted sets under the listpack threshold are unaffected either way, since they never used the skiplist encoding to begin with.

The numbers below compare only the ordered index: skiplist versus fbtree, with the hashtable and member embedding unchanged.

According to recent reports, inserting 5 million 20-byte members sequentially reduced per-member memory overhead, excluding the member data itself, from 50.3B to 28.5B, a 43% reduction. The same 5 million members inserted in random order reduced per-member overhead from 50.3B to 32.0B, a 36% reduction.

The smaller reduction comes from random insertion leaving more partially filled nodes than sequential insertion.

For the 5-million-member set in this test, that is roughly 109 MB saved with sequential inserts and 92 MB with random inserts. The savings are per member, not per byte stored, so the relative reduction in total memory is largest for sets with many small members and shrinks as member size grows.

According to recent reports, the benchmarks below were measured on PR #4206’s oi/pr3-fbtree-v2 branch and were not rerun for the merged commit. They were run on a Graviton3 c7g.metal system with 64 cores, nine I/O threads, a pipeline depth of 10, and a 3-million-member sorted set. Each test was repeated five times; the reported confidence intervals were ≤2% for all commands except ZRANDMEMBER.

The same underlying design changes also improve throughput for several sorted set operations:.

ZADD and ZREM reposition elements in the tree, so they gain the most from fbtree's shallower structure and fewer pointer updates. Range operations see smaller gains because once the index traversal becomes cheap, producing and returning the requested elements becomes a larger part of the total cost. ZSCORE and ZRANDMEMBER barely move because they use the hashtable, not the ordered index.

The important takeaway: the commands didn't change, but in our tests large sorted sets carried 36–43% less per-member overhead, and ZADD and ZREM throughput rose 105% and 76%.

The goal wasn't simply to make the data structure faster in isolation: the implementation was repeatedly benchmarked against the existing skiplist through the full Valkey server, with optimizations added until fbtree matched or exceeded the skiplist across the tested sorted set commands.

Recent findings suggest that valkey 9.2 is presently in release-candidate testing. Before GA, try the 9.2 release candidate with your real workload, especially if large sorted sets or commands such as ZADD, ZREM, ZRANK, or ZCOUNT are notable to you. Your testing and feedback can help surface issues before the final release, so open an matter with anything you find.
